Pleasure
plezh'ur
n. (delight, good will, that which pleases; rendering Hebrew chephets and ratson, Greek eudokia and hedone)
From the French plaisir, from the Latin placeo, to please. Hebrew chephets means delight and also purpose — what one takes pleasure in is what one determines to do — and the Authorized Version's good pleasure preserves this fusion of delight and decree.

Biblical Definition

Pleasure in Scripture is first God's and only then man's, and the order matters. The creation exists for it: “for thy pleasure they are and were created” (Revelation 4:11). Election rests on it: God predestinated us unto the adoption of children “according to the good pleasure of his will” (Ephesians 1:5), which locates the cause of salvation in God's delight rather than in anything foreseen in the creature. Most searchingly, the atonement is traced to it: “Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief” (Isaiah 53:10) — not that the Father took delight in the Son's agony as agony, but that the redemption accomplished through it was his settled purpose and joy. Because the Hebrew word fuses delight and determination, God's pleasure is never a mood; it is his will, and it shall stand. Man's pleasure is treated more carefully. Scripture is not ascetic — God giveth us richly all things to enjoy — but it names the disordering of pleasure as a mark of the last days, when men shall be “lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God” (2 Timothy 3:4). The fault there is not that pleasure is loved but that it is loved more, and a good put in God's place becomes an idol.

Webster 1828 Definition

Delight, and also settled good will. God's good pleasure fuses delight with decree — creation, election, and even the bruising of the Servant are traced to it; man's pleasure is good until loved above God.

expand to see more

PLEASURE, n. plezh'ur. [Fr. plaisir; L. placeo, to please.] The gratification of the senses or of the mind; agreeable sensations or emotions; delight.

2. Approbation; as, it is the pleasure of the court.

3. Arbitrary will or choice; as, he may go or stay at his pleasure.

4. Sensual gratification; voluptuousness — often in a bad sense.

5. In Scripture, the good pleasure of God, his sovereign will and delight; as, according to the good pleasure of his will, Eph. 1.

Key Scripture

Revelation 4:11 — "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created."

Ephesians 1:5 — "Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,"

Isaiah 53:10 — "Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand."

2 Timothy 3:4 — "Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God;"

Modern Corruption

Modern life treats pleasure as the measure of a good life and Christianity as its enemy. Scripture makes pleasure a creature — genuinely good, God's own before it is ours, and ruinous only when it displaces him.

expand to see more

The world's error is to make pleasure ultimate, which destroys it; the pursuit of sensation apart from God yields the diminishing returns Ecclesiastes catalogued three thousand years ago. But the church has often answered with an asceticism Scripture does not teach, treating enjoyment itself as suspect and producing a piety that is grim rather than holy. Paul names the forbidding of meats and marriage as a doctrine of devils, and the same Psalm that speaks of God's presence promises pleasures for evermore at his right hand.

The doctrinal centre of the word is God's good pleasure, and this is where the sharpest correction falls on a man-centred gospel. Ephesians 1:5 grounds adoption in the good pleasure of God's will — not in foreseen faith, not in the sinner's decision, not in anything but God's delight in doing it. Isaiah 53:10 pushes further than most are comfortable going, saying it pleased the LORD to bruise him. The principle to recover is that God's pleasure is the deepest cause of everything, including the cross, and that a creature's pleasures are rightly ordered only when they run toward the God whose pleasure made them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chephets is delight and purpose together; ratson is good pleasure or acceptance. Greek eudokia is good pleasure or benevolent will, while hedone is pleasure in the sensual sense, giving English hedonism.

expand to see more

Hebrew chephets (H2656) — delight, desire, purpose; the pleasure of the LORD that shall prosper.

Hebrew ratson (H7522) — goodwill, favour, acceptable will; what is acceptable to God.

Greek eudokia (G2107) — good pleasure, benevolent purpose; the ground of election in Ephesians 1:5.

Greek thelema (G2307) — will; joined to eudokia in the phrase good pleasure of his will.

Greek hedone (G2237) — pleasure, sensual delight; the root of English hedonism.

Usage

"Of creation's final cause: for thy pleasure they are and were created (Revelation 4:11)."

"Of election grounded in God's delight: according to the good pleasure of his will (Ephesians 1:5)."

"Of pleasure disordered by being loved above God: lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God (2 Timothy 3:4)."
